column1: # FIX-1187 — office-promotion manifest (shape B), SET 2, VERSION 2.
# THIS FILE IS AN AUTHORISATION. It SUPERSEDES
# docs/audits/2026-09-16-fix1187-office-promotion-manifest.tsv.
# WHY A NEW FILE RATHER THAN AN EDIT. cc-130 stopped set 2 at its pre-write
# check because the 2026-09-16 manifest had gone DEAD, not merely blocked: the
# nightly promotion of 2026-09-17 23:20:46 UTC deleted Marshall's survivor row
# (27090d3a), which that file names as a survivor UUID. A manifest is an
# authorisation, and an authorisation that names a row which no longer exists
# cannot be corrected in place and stay an authorisation. The old file keeps its
# SUPERSEDED comment and is not deleted.
# WHAT CHANGED, in one line: FIVE rows became FOUR. Marshall is gone from the
# set.
# WHY MARSHALL IS NOT HERE. The same promotion that killed his manifest row also
# merged his Senate stub's money onto the promoted row, and cc-131's FIX-1195
# restore (2026-09-18 02:42 UTC) put S0KS00315 back as that row's live
# fec_candidate_id with H6KS01179 in prior_fec_candidate_ids. So 60f87348 is
# already an elected Senator holding a Senate id with the Senate money
# ($11,374,334 across 4,867 FR rows) — which is exactly what a set-2 row is for.
# There is no Senate stub left to merge. Re-deriving the census on prod
# confirms it: the keyed shape-B query now returns exactly these FOUR and
# Marshall is absent.
# RE-DERIVED ON PROD 2026-09-18 02:47 UTC. Every active elected row whose
# role_title is Senator and whose live fec_candidate_id carries an H prefix,
# joined to a tier='candidate' "Candidate for Senator" row of the same person
# (surname, first name, and the CAND_ID's state characters) holding an S id with
# live FR rows. Exactly four. The survivor UUIDs and both ids per row are
# UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-16 derivation for all four — only Marshall moved.
# PROD STATE READ 2026-09-18 02:5x UTC, all twelve rows:
#   survivor (elected Senator, holds the HOUSE id)      FR rows   official_donor_totals
#     Gary C. Peters     efd0cd51  H8MI09068              2,240    $5,689,033
#     John R. Curtis     0fcc1b87  H8UT03238              3,215    $7,761,678
#     Cynthia M. Lummis  a911c906  H8WY00148                845    $2,798,905
#   senate stub (candidate, holds the SENATE id and the live money)
#     Gary Peters        cdc8ae79  S4MI00355             23,464   $27,906,385
#     Cynthia Lummis     60bfd339  S0WY00137              1,852    $3,951,283
#   house stub — ALREADY MERGED BY SET 1, listed for cross-reference ONLY
#     41d2af4c / b05ae301 / 71a323fc / 12b08a65 each now carry
#     {"merged_fec_candidate_ids": [<the house id>]} and ZERO FR rows.
#   Set 1 is therefore confirmed complete for all four, which is the
#   precondition the 2026-09-16 file spelled out as "SET 1 MUST RUN BEFORE
#   SET 2" (two stubs for one survivor would violate
#   financial_relationships_relcycle_unique, because _manifest is
#   (survivor PRIMARY KEY, dup UNIQUE) and the merge SQL assumes 1:1).
# TOTAL TO MOVE: 46,798 stub FR rows.
# WHAT A ROW AUTHORISES, in one transaction:
#   1. survivor.source_ids.fec_candidate_id      <- current_id (the SENATE id)
#      survivor.source_ids.prior_fec_candidate_ids += prior_id (the HOUSE id)
#   2. merge senate_stub into survivor as an ordinary pair on current_id
#   3. retire current_id on senate_stub (fec_candidate_id -> merged_fec_candidate_ids)
# EVIDENCE. Every Senate id was verified against the OpenFEC API on 2026-09-16
# (https://api.open.fec.gov/v1/candidate/<ID>/); the evidence column carries the
# returned name / state / office_full / party verbatim, and a row with an empty
# evidence column is REFUSED by the script. Shape B rewrites an identity, not
# just money, so the authorisation has to be per-row and checkable. Nothing
# about those four candidacies changed between 09-16 and 09-18, and the ids
# themselves are unchanged, so the 09-16 verification stands.
# NOT YET APPLIED. cc-131 derived and committed this file but did NOT run set 2:
# its drain-and-wait window is Saturday 2026-09-19 ~12:00-21:30 UTC and the
# session was Friday 09-18 ~03:00 UTC. cc-132 applies it after repeating cc-131's
# read 7 in full. The point of committing it unapplied is that cc-132 then
# applies a REVIEWED file rather than deriving one under time pressure.
